overview.headline: Understanding drag and how the drag equation combines flow conditions and shape

keyPoints.point: Drag depends on air density and the square of velocity along with viscosity, compressibility, size, shape and inclination.
keyPoints.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity, the air’s viscosity and compressibility, the size and shape of the body

keyPoints.point: The drag equation relates drag to drag coefficient, density, velocity squared and reference area.
keyPoints.quote: drag D is equal to the drag coefficient Cd times the density rho (ρ) times half of the velocity V squared times the reference area A

keyPoints.point: The drag coefficient bundles form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag and induced drag into a single value.
keyPoints.quote: The drag coefficient given above includes form drag, skin friction drag, wave drag, and induced drag components.

keyPoints.point: Drag coefficients are determined experimentally in a wind tunnel for given air conditions and shape.
keyPoints.quote: Drag coefficients are almost always determined experimentally using a wind tunnel.

keyPoints.point: The reference area can be total surface area, frontal area or wing area and changes the coefficient value while drag stays the same.
keyPoints.quote: If we think of drag as being caused by friction between the air and the body, a logical choice would be the total surface area of the body.

keyTerms.gloss: aerodynamic force opposing motion that depends on density, velocity, viscosity and shape
keyTerms.quote: Drag depends on the density of the air, the square of the velocity, the air’s viscosity and compressibility

keyTerms.gloss: single variable that collects complex effects of shape, inclination and viscosity into the drag equation
keyTerms.quote: For drag, this variable is called the drag coefficient, designated “Cd.”

keyTerms.gloss: chosen area that characterizes size dependence in the drag and lift force equations
keyTerms.quote: Notice that the area (A) given in the drag equation is given as a reference area.

keyTerms.gloss: mass per volume of air designated by the Greek letter rho in the equation
keyTerms.quote: In the equation given above, the density is designated by the letter rho (ρ).

keyTerms.gloss: combined term of density times velocity squared divided by two that appears in Bernoulli pressure equation
keyTerms.quote: The combination of terms “density times the square of the velocity divided by two” is called the dynamic pressure
